content.overview: Section 72 permits a holder of securities to nominate a person to whom the securities are to vest on the holder's death, subject to the prescribed manner and statutory conditions. It also addresses joint holders and a nominee who is a minor. The legal effect of nomination in relation to succession and beneficial ownership must be stated in light of binding authority, not inferred from the section alone.
content.glance: Section 72 permits a holder of securities to nominate a person to whom the securities are to vest on the holder's death, subject to the prescribed manner and statutory conditions. It also addresses joint holders and a nominee who is a minor. The legal effect of nomination in relation to succession and beneficial ownership must be stated in light of binding authority, not inferred from the section alone.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 72 (Nomination). A holder of securities may nominate, in the prescribed manner, a person to whom the securities are to vest on the holder's death. Joint holders may make a nomination together. The section provides for variation or cancellation of a nomination and for appointment of a person to receive the securities where the nominee is a minor. The company may require evidence before registering a person as holder following the death. Do not state that nomination by itself conclusively defeats testamentary succession or determines beneficial ownership without applying binding Supreme Court authority and the relevant facts. Section 59 is a distinct rectification route where its requirements are met. This topic remains under statutory-rule and case-law review.

sections.heading: Nomination
sections.body: A holder of securities may nominate, in the prescribed manner, a person to whom the securities are to vest on the holder's death.

sections.heading: Joint holders
sections.body: Where securities are held by more than one person jointly, the joint holders may nominate a person in the prescribed manner.

sections.heading: Variation, cancellation and minor nominee
sections.body: A nomination may be varied or cancelled in the prescribed manner. The section also permits the holder to appoint a person in the prescribed manner to become entitled where the nominee is a minor and the holder dies while the nominee remains a minor. Check the applicable rules for form and procedure.

sections.heading: Transmission and registration
sections.body: Following the holder's death, the nominee's claim and any registration of the securities must be processed under section 72, the applicable rules and the company's requirements for evidence. Do not infer that nomination alone conclusively determines beneficial ownership or overrides succession law without applying binding authority.

sections.heading: Separate rectification route
sections.body: Section 59 concerns rectification of the register where its statutory conditions are met. It is a distinct route and should not be presented as an automatic consequence of every nomination dispute.

examples.title: Nominee is a minor
examples.body: Check whether the holder appointed a person in the prescribed manner to become entitled if the holder dies while the nominee remains a minor, and verify the applicable rule requirements.

hypotheticals.question: A securities holder nominates a person and later changes the nomination. Which issues must be checked after the holder's death?
hypotheticals.analysis: Verify the latest valid nomination and compliance with the prescribed manner; check whether joint-holder or minor-nominee provisions apply; then assess registration/transmission and any succession or beneficial-ownership dispute under binding authority. Do not treat the nomination as automatically conclusive of every succession issue.

hypotheticals.question: A nominee asks the company to register the securities after the holder's death, while another person asserts a succession claim. What is the proper analysis?
hypotheticals.analysis: Apply section 72 and its rules to the nomination and registration request, then separately analyse the competing succession/beneficial-ownership claim under binding authority and the facts. Section 59 may be relevant if its statutory requirements for rectification are met; it is not automatic.

misconceptions.trap: Treating nomination as conclusively determining beneficial ownership or defeating every succession claim.
misconceptions.correction: Analyse section 72 together with binding authority and the facts; do not infer a conclusive succession rule from the nomination wording alone.

misconceptions.trap: Ignoring prescribed form, variation/cancellation or the minor-nominee mechanism.
misconceptions.correction: Check the Act and applicable rules for the valid nomination, its variation/cancellation and any appointment where the nominee is a minor.

misconceptions.trap: Treating section 59 rectification as an automatic remedy in every nomination dispute.
misconceptions.correction: Section 59 is a distinct remedy and applies only where its statutory conditions are satisfied.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does section 72 provide?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: It permits nomination of a person to whom securities are to vest on the holder's death, subject to the prescribed manner and statutory conditions.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Does nomination alone conclusively settle all succession and beneficial-ownership disputes?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Do not assume so. Apply binding authority and the facts to the statutory nomination and any competing succession claim.
